# Change Data Capture

## When to Use This Skill

- Push entity data changes to a data lake, warehouse or any Kafka consumer
- Read what a project already streams, and to which topics
- Add or remove a tracked entity, attribute or association
- Work out why a topic is empty, or why its name changed

CDC is **publish-only**. Mendix 11.16 has no model for subscribing to another
app's CDC stream — `ChangeDataCapture` has exactly one document type and no
consumed counterpart. To *read* another app's data, use `odata.consume`
(external entities), `rest.consumed`, or the external database connector
(`database-connection`, `sql.generate`) against whatever the lake exposes.

## Commands

```sql
mdl 1;
list change data capture services;
list change data capture services in MyModule;
describe change data capture service Module.OrdersCDCService;

create or modify change data capture service Module.OrdersCDCService
(
  ServiceName: 'OrdersCDCService'
)
{
  entity Module.Order (
    OrderId,
    CustomerName,
    Price as 'Amount',        -- exposed name only when it differs
    Order_Customer            -- an association of this entity
  );
  entity Module.Customer as 'Client' (CustomerId, Address);
};

drop change data capture service Module.OrdersCDCService;
```

**Needs Mendix 11.10+.** Below that the project cannot store the baseline
(`ChangeDataCapture$VersionedEntityChangeDataCaptureService`), and `check`
refuses with MDL-VERSION01 before anything is written.

## Members Are Named, Not Typed

A member resolves to an attribute **or** an association of that entity, and its
CDC type comes from the domain model. Attributes are looked at first; a name
that is both is a check error rather than a guess.

| Mendix attribute type | CDC type |
|---|---|
| Binary, Boolean, DateTime, Decimal | the same name |
| Date | `DateTime` (Mendix has no date-only type) |
| Enumeration | `Enumeration` |
| Integer | `Int32` |
| Long, AutoNumber | `Int64` |
| String, HashedString | `String` |
| an association | `ArrayOfInt64` |

Measured from Studio Pro's own CDC editor, which mxbuild ships as readable
JavaScript — not inferred. Those are every Mendix attribute type, so nothing is
unmappable.

Two rules the editor enforces and so does `check`:

- **`id` is implicit and must not be listed.** Studio Pro shows it as a checked,
  disabled row but stores no property for it; the object id reaches a consumer
  from the runtime's change envelope, not from the model.
- **An association is tracked from its FROM entity** — the one that owns the
  foreign key — and the entity at its other end must be tracked too. An
  association both sides own (`owner Both`) is tracked from **both** entities:
  name it in each entity's member list, or mxbuild refuses the service (CE1583).
  `check -p` reports either gap as MDL-CDC01 (ako/mxcli#2613).

Only **persistable** entities can be tracked. A view entity or an external
entity has no rows of its own, so there is nothing to capture; both are refused.
(A view entity reports `Persistable = true`, so the refusal is on its source,
not that flag.)

## The Topic, and Why a Major Bump Is Expensive

```
cdc.<AppName>.<ExposedName>.<Major>.<space>
```

Every segment but the last is a model value. `AppName` comes from the project
and is **not settable from MDL** — changing it would re-point every topic the
service publishes to. `<space>` is the `BusinessEvents.EventBrokerSpace`
constant at runtime.

So a **major version bump starts a new topic**, and downstream that is a new
table with no history. The same is true of renaming an entity's exposed name.
`describe` prints each source's revision next to its topic for exactly this
reason:

```
-- entity CdcPublish.Order
--   revision 1.1   topic cdc.TestApp.Order.1.{space}
--   attribute   CdcPublish.Order.OrderId   [Int64]
--   association CdcPublish.Order_Customer   [ArrayOfInt64]
```

## What You Author, and What Is Computed

Only the **live side**. The document also holds a **baseline** — the frozen copy
Studio Pro's *accept changes* writes — and mxcli rebuilds it from the domain
model on every write. You cannot author it, by design:

the baseline identifies what it tracks by **GUID**, and the runtime keys
`mendixsystem$entity.id` and `mendixsystem$attribute.id` on those values. A
wrong GUID detaches an entity from its table and destroys its rows on the next
deploy, with no build error and nothing in a diff to see. A GUID an author could
write is a GUID an author could get wrong, so MDL has no syntax for one.

Consequences worth knowing:

- `create or modify` rebuilds the whole document, and storage elides the write
  when the result matches what is stored — so re-running an unchanged script
  reports `Unchanged`, not a churn.
- Running it over a **Studio Pro-authored** service also reports `Unchanged`:
  mxcli's output is byte-identical to Studio Pro's. If it ever says `Modified`
  on a service nobody touched, something has drifted — investigate rather than
  accept it.
- mxbuild reports CE1585 when the two sides disagree, and CE1577 on an empty
  `AppName`. From **Mendix 11.17** the baseline also records the project's
  decimal scale and, per member, its multiplicity, nullability and String length
  (ako/mxcli#2612); mxcli derives them from the domain model as Studio Pro's
  editor does, and a change to one is a major version bump. An *absent* baseline is worse than either: `mx check` crashes with
  `The given key '<guid>' was not present in the dictionary`.

## Version Policy — Inferred, Not Measured

On modify:

| change to a source | result |
|---|---|
| nothing | keeps its stored version |
| a member added | minor + 1 |
| a member removed, an exposed name renamed, or a type changed | **major + 1**, minor 0 |
| a brand-new source | starts at 1.0, and does not bump the service |

The service takes the largest bump any source took.

**This rule is inferred from one Studio Pro document.** mxbuild ignores version
numbers entirely, so a wrong rule never fails a build — it quietly moves a
topic. If you can, add, rename and remove a property in Studio Pro, accept the
changes, and compare: a disagreement means this table is wrong.

## Verifying the Whole Chain

`mx check` passing proves the document is valid, not that anything is published.
For that you need a broker and a running app. Verified end to end against
[DuckGraphLake](https://github.com/ako/DuckGraphLake), which serves a Kafka
endpoint and writes each topic to an Iceberg table:

```bash
duckgraphlake ~/lake
```

Two constants are **mandatory** — without either, the app does not merely
consume nothing, it **fails to boot** (`StartupBusinessEvents` throws in the
after-startup action):

```bash
mxcli constant set BusinessEvents.ServerUrl 127.0.0.1:9092 -p app.mpr
```

```bash
mxcli constant set BusinessEvents.EventBrokerSpace local -p app.mpr
```

They are stored per-machine in gitignored `.mxcli/constants.json`, so nothing
reaches version control.

```bash
mxcli run --local --detach --db-type hsqldb --runtime-setting Kafka.BootstrapServers=127.0.0.1:9092 -p app.mpr
```

Then commit a tracked object and look. The runtime publishes within a second:

```bash
psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U lake -d lake -c 'select * from testapp."order"'
```

What the log should show, in order:

```
Change Data Capture Publisher: Elected as active producer - starting CDC producer worker
Change Data Capture Publisher: Snapshot decision: 2 entities to snapshot (2 changed, 0 forced)
```

Three things that cost time to learn:

- **`--db-type hsqldb` is enough.** CDC publishes normally on it. The runtime
  warns `SystemPropertyManager.supportsUpdate is false; snapshot overlap
  protection is degraded` — that is not a failure and PostgreSQL is not needed.
- **A snapshot is sent once per revision.** The first boot against an empty
  database snapshots nothing, and the next boot logs `skipping N unchanged`. Data
  created before the app first ran against that broker never arrives: start with
  an empty database, or a fresh lake folder.
- **Mendix 11.14+ needs JDK 25.** On 21 the runtime refuses to start.

## Checklist

- [ ] Project is Mendix 11.10 or later
- [ ] Every tracked entity is **persistable** — not a view or external entity
- [ ] `id` is not in any member list
- [ ] No two sources share an exposed name (they would share a topic)
- [ ] `AppName` is not in the property list
- [ ] After a modify, `describe` shows the revisions and topics you expect — a
      major bump means a **new topic** and a new table downstream
- [ ] `mxcli check -p app.mpr` passes before `exec`
- [ ] Re-running an unchanged script reports `Unchanged`
- [ ] For a real check, boot the app against a broker and look for the rows;
      a valid document publishes nothing if the two constants are unset
